> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> WID.world was GATED until 2026-07-28 — 124,367,162 observations across 2,465,197 series held locally and served to nobody — because the site publishes no licence text and re-hosting on assumption was not acceptable. Resolved: WID declares CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 via a rel="license" link on its chart, and granted written permission on 2026-07-27 for educational re-hosting. That grant came with a condition — "keep the most updated data sources" — so this fetcher is part of the permission, not an optimisation. One CSV per country/region (424 files, ~7 GB total), each fetched, parsed and merged independently so memory is bounded by the largest country and one failure cannot cost the rest.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: SHA-256 over the whole bulk_download directory listing (every filename, timestamp and size). Watching the LISTING rather than a fixed file means a newly ADDED country is itself a change signal — the failure a pinned URL caused on yale_epi, where an entire new edition went unnoticed (ledger R78).

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/wid.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/wid.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
World Inequality Database (WID.world) — bulk distribution, per-country files.

LICENCE: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, declared by WID's own `rel="license"` link on the chart at
wid.world/world/ (the site publishes no licence TEXT anywhere — /data/, /methodology/,
/website-credits/, the privacy policy and the bulk README were all checked rendered).
Re-hosted with written permission from WID.world dated 2026-07-27, which came with a
condition: "we invite you to keep the most updated data sources". This fetcher is how
that promise is kept — without it the re-hosted copy is a snapshot we agreed not to
serve. See DATABASE_LICENSES_VERBATIM.md for the verbatim evidence.

LAYOUT. WID ships one CSV per country/region at wid.world/bulk_download/
(424 of them, ~17 MB each, semicolon-separated). The store mirrors that shape one
parquet per country, so each file is fetched, parsed and merged INDEPENDENTLY:
memory stays bounded by the largest single country rather than by the ~7 GB total,
and a country that fails cannot cost the other 423. There is a
`WID_fulldataset_.zip` but it is a 7,116-byte placeholder last touched in 2020 — not
the full dataset its name promises.

KEYS. `WID:{variable}:{percentile}:{age}:{pop}:{country}`, verified against the
published store: 8,731 of 8,731 ids reproduced exactly for OA-PPP. Dates are
period-END (12-31), this source's existing convention.

BUDGET. A full refresh is ~7 GB, which does not fit a CI run. The vintage below moves
only when WID republishes, so the expensive path is rare; and within a run a wall-clock
budget stops cleanly and reports PARTIAL rather than being killed at the job ceiling.

RESUME. The budget is only useful if the next run continues where this one stopped,
and that does not happen for free: the loop walks sorted(rows) from the top every
time, so with nothing to skip it re-fetches the same early countries forever and the
end of the alphabet is unreachable at ANY budget. Proven, not assumed — with the
marker disabled, three runs fetched AA / AA,BB,CC / AA,BB,CC and stalled at 3 of 8
countries; with it, 1 then 4 then 7 of 8. `_country_vintage.json` records the
listing's own (last-modified|size) per country once its merge has landed, so a run
skips what is already at the published vintage and spends its budget on what is not.
```

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='wid'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source wid --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source wid --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('wid');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source wid
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `wid`.*

- **root cause**: `code_bug`  (confidence high)
- **which units**: Nothing upstream is failing. All 12 named sub-units (Al, ON, ON-MER, OO-MER, OP-MER, OQ-MER, SW, XQ, XQ-MER, XC, XE, XK — the "+6 more" are SW, XQ, XQ-MER, XC, XE, XK) return HTTP 200 with a CSV header and zero data rows. They are 47 bytes (9 of them) or 60 bytes (XC/XE/XK), against 45-65 MB for a real country. 412 of 424 country files parsed and merged normally on the one run that happened (412 stamped in _country_vintage.json, 412 per-country parquets on disk). 0 of 424 are genuinely broken.
- **blast radius**: 0 observations lost — the 12 entities hold no data upstream to lose. But the source-level effect was total: DefinitiveError sank the whole run, so wid's ONE AND ONLY attempt ever (runs.id=395, 2026-08-02T02:50:16Z, 2129.7 s) recorded status=partial obs=0, source_state has no wid row at all, last_success is unstamped, and series_cursor holds 0 rows for wid — so ~2.47M served series show as never refreshed despite 412 country files having actually merged.
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> Do not chase the reported error — it is already fixed and un-rerun. Two actions, in order.
> 
> (1) RE-RUN wid and let the current code report. It is run_location: local (updater/registry.yaml:6197ff), so tools/run_local_heavy.ps1. This alone converts the stale 'schema/structural break' into the truth. But do (2) FIRST, because the very next run attempts only the 12 empties and will raise.
> 
> (2) Fix the empty-entity bookkeeping in updater/strategies/fetchers/wid.py. The empty branch (lines 222-226) must record the entity the way the merged branch does, and the skip gate at line 185 must not demand a parquet for an entity that legitimately has none (`blob.exists(path)` is False for 11 of the 12, so a stamp alone will not skip them). Concretely: stamp a distinguishable value, e.g. `done[country] = f"{_mod}|{_size}|empty"`, set `dirty = True`, and let the gate skip on either form — requiring `blob.exists(path)` only for the non-empty form. WID's own (last-modified|size) then re-checks each entity exactly when it is republished, which is the only moment it could gain data. Verified outcome: attempted drops to 0 and finalize() returns status='no_change' / 'no new rows' (ran it) instead of raising.
> 
> Defensively, also make the empty-window gate in updater/strategies/fetchers/_common.py:270 mean what it says — 'the source went dark' — rather than 'every unit we happened to attempt is one we already know is header-only'. Excluding known-empty units from that denominator is better than raising wid's empty_window_floor; a bare floor bump to 12 also returns 'no_change' (verified) but silently re-arms the moment WID publishes a 13th empty entity.
> 
> Nothing here is upstream. WID answered every request 200, first byte to last, with no Retry-After and no throttling.

Range-probed (bytes=0-399, HTTP 206) FR (Content-Range bytes 0-399/68161470), US (/52574299), ZA (/45417668), DE-BY (/1168) — all now header `country;variable;percentile;year;value;age;pop;data_quality`, while QC (Last-Modified 2025-08-07) still has the 7-column header. ## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
